newsitem.title: FRANCE: French navy takes over nuclear aircraft-carrier.
newsitem.headline: French navy takes over nuclear aircraft-carrier.

text.p: The French navy took delivery of its first nuclear-powered aircraft carrier on Saturday, a half-fnished ship due to go into operation in more than two years' time as the future pride of the fleet.

In a ceremony in Brest in western France, the Charles de Gaulle officially became a naval vessel rather than a maritime building site when captain Richard Wilmot-Roussel was handed control from the Directorate of Naval Constructions (DCN).
"This is a very important moment for the crew," Wilmot-Roussel said.
About 800 sailors will start living abroad the vessel, floating in port, and take responsibility for security during two years of continuing fittings and tests.
The first atomic-powered surface vessel in the French fleet will get its nuclear unit in October. Once completed in the second half of 1999, it will have a crew of 2,000 and between 35 and 40 planes.
The carrier, displacing 40,500 tonnes fully-loaded with a 260-metre (285-yard) long flight deck, is to replace the carrier Clemenceau, due to be withdrawn from active service this year.
Facing sweeping defence budget cuts after the Cold War, France has yet to decide whether to build a sister for the Charles de Gaulle to replace its other ageing carrier, the Foch.
